zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價與Fed紀錄推升中天期殖利率，標售買盤支撐長端

油價續漲，6月Fed會議紀錄也顯示升息仍是選項，美債殖利率週三再度上升。不過，賣壓比週二溫和，主要集中在5年期，殖利率上升4個基點至4.31%；10年期在$390億增額標售需求強勁的支撐下，僅上升1個基點至4.56%。

美伊停火動搖，布蘭特原油上漲5.21%，偏低的成品油庫存則讓市場更難承受供應中斷。Fed紀錄顯示，雖然6月決議全票維持利率不變，少數官員當時已認為有理由升息。貨幣市場將下一次預期升息提前至10月，但10年期損益兩平通膨率仍停在2.25%，指標殖利率的小幅上升完全來自實質利率。

殖利率提高後，市場仍有投資人願意承接存續期間。美債標售得標殖利率低於發行前交易水準，美股也收復大部分盤中跌幅。信用保護成本雖然升高，私募債、有資產擔保的貸款與專門融資結構仍提供資金管道。財務困難的企業卻面對另一種市場：Aston Martin債價下跌、債權人聯合行動，Victoria則提出重整方案，不接受交換的債權人可能蒙受重大損失。

## 升息預期提前，5年期美債承壓最重

2年期殖利率上升2個基點至4.21%，5年期上升4個基點至4.31%，10年與30年期各上升1個基點，分別收在4.56%及5.06%。2年與10年期、2年與30年期利差均收窄1個基點，至35及85個基點。相較前一天全面走弱，週三更明顯的是5年期表現落後，而非長端殖利率再次大幅跳升。

10年期實質殖利率上升1個基點至2.31%，損益兩平通膨率維持2.25%。5年期實質殖利率同樣上升1個基點至2.00%，7年期維持2.14%，20年與30年期分別上升1及2個基點，至2.66%及2.86%。油價改變了市場對Fed的預期，卻未推高當日10年期通膨補償。

6月16日至17日會議紀錄指出，物價上行風險仍高，就業下行風險略為減輕。少數與會者認為有理由升息，但全體仍同意將聯邦基金利率區間維持在3.5%至3.75%。九位官員預測2026年至少升息25個基點，其中六位預期至少升息兩次；另九位預期不變或降息。主席Kevin Warsh未提交預測。

委員會並未認定升息勢在必行。多數官員認為，若通膨降溫，可以維持利率，甚至最終降息；但若AI帶動的需求、能源及關稅使物價持續過快上升，多數人也認為可能需要進一步緊縮。他們仍預期實質經濟穩健成長、勞動市場穩定。新一輪敵對行動讓通膨風險更加迫近，市場因而將下一次預期升息提前至10月。

美國空襲與對伊朗石油銷售的限制，使能源前景轉差。WTI上漲4.37%至$73.52，布蘭特盤中突破$79，收在$78.02。截至7月3日的一週，美國商業原油庫存增加300萬桶，但汽油減少190萬桶、蒸餾油減少500萬桶。煉油廠產能利用率已達95.8%，蒸餾油庫存仍比五年同期平均低約12%。原油增庫並不足以消除成品油供應吃緊的疑慮。

美國內需資料則呈現不同方向。5月批發銷售增加3.4%至$8,174億，4月增幅上修至2.2%；庫存僅增加0.1%至$9,418億，庫存銷售比降至1.15，低於一年前的1.31。相對庫存而言，銷售仍強，但名目金額本身無法區分銷量與價格各自的貢獻。

消費信貸明顯減速。5月總額經季調年率變化為零，4月修正後仍增4.9%。循環信貸以年率計萎縮4.7%，非循環信貸成長1.6%，信貸餘額合計$5.1545兆。信用卡借款下降，使高利率下的消費韌性出現疑問，只是當天交易焦點仍在油價與Fed。

### 殖利率讓利吸引指標券買盤

$390億10年期增額標售的得標殖利率為4.580%，比發行前交易水準低約0.6個基點，投標倍數2.59。間接投標人取得$317.21億、直接投標人$41.75億、交易商$30.27億。該券剩餘天期9年10個月，7月15日交割。投資人需求限制了指標券跌幅，但未帶動整體市場反彈。

財政部另發行$720億119天期國庫券，最高利率3.790%，投標倍數3.41。間接投標人取得$489.86億，直接投標人$31.58億，交易商$182.27億，7月14日交割。次級市場17週期殖利率上升2個基點至3.89%，4、6及8週期則下跌。現金部位的配置需求仍強，與較受政策路徑影響的中短天期債券走弱形成差別。

## 信用買方更挑剔，借款人尋找不同融資管道

停火破裂後，信用違約交換利差擴大。LQD下跌0.19%、HYG下跌0.13%、JNK下跌0.16%，相較油價再次大漲，跌幅仍有限。偏緊的信用估值缺乏承受事件風險的緩衝，但更廣泛的投資策略與融資結構，仍讓借款人有機會取得資金。

美國非傳統債券基金資產規模在2026年成長約6%，較2024年底增加18%；歐洲全球彈性債券基金今年也成長近10%。這類經理人可以避開昂貴的指標成分，尋找其他債券，為發行人提供不同的買盤來源，也讓個別券種的選擇更加重要。

中東借款人則轉向私募。中東歐、中東及非洲的2026年私募發行量達約$330億，約為去年同期的十倍，其中中東主權、企業及金融機構占約三分之二。Qatar Energy在6月完成的$35億交易，顯示非公開市場也能提供大額資金。不過，快速執行與保密性並非免費：上半年私募平均票息5.12%，高於國際市場發售新興債的3.18%，反映流動性較低所需的補償，而非融資更便宜。

新出爐的研究則估算了前一天Amazon供給的影響。美銀分析師Yuri Seliger與Sohyun Marie Lee估計，交易使既有大型雲端業者債券利差擴大6至15個基點，並對週二10年期美債殖利率升幅貢獻8個基點。後者是分析師估算的影響，並非官方單日變化的逐項拆解。Amazon約$410億訂單相當於$250億發行額的1.6倍，低於2月交易的4.7倍。公司今年已發債逾$900億，納入大型雲端業者合計$1,940億的統計；這個範圍比先前全球AI相關債券的廣義統計更窄。

### 完工資產支持借款，困境企業則須讓出債權價值

Blackstone旗下QTS尋求$20億資金，用於美國資料中心債務再融資及支付股利。其中$10億定期貸款以99至99.5的價格招攬投資人，利差225至250個基點，另搭配$10億擔保債務。擔保品是12座已完工、全數出租給三家投資級大型雲端業者的資料中心。借款依據是營運資產已簽約的現金流，而非尚未完成的建設與未來需求。

Cantor Fitzgerald為Seer Capital安排一筆擬議中的$3億First Abu Dhabi Bank融資，用於購買重大風險移轉工具，並由投資級保險擔保支持。融資超過投資淨資產價值的50%，可支持連結至少$40億銀行貸款的曝險。保險降低了融資成本，但底層工具承擔貸款組合5%至15%的損失；加上槓桿後，投資結果更依賴貸款表現及擔保的可靠程度。

Aston Martin債權人面對的情況更艱難。持有逾半數優先擔保票據的臨時債權人小組簽署合作協議，當時獲利壓力正使債價下跌。公司$10.5億、2029年到期擔保票據跌至面額約72%，週三下跌約4個百分點。優先擔保地位無法阻擋營運惡化對價格的影響，回收價值與債權人的談判位置愈來愈重要。

Victoria向接受方案的2028年票據持有人提出，以原債權價值75%換取2031年到期的第二順位新債，並給予約19%股權。重整擬減少逾£3億債務與特別股負擔，不同意的持有人則面臨債權歸零。公司爭取到的財務空間，來自債權與所有權重新分配，而非單純以較高票息換取更長期限。

倫敦保險連結證券市場另有一筆已完成的交易。英國洪水保險最後承擔者Flood Re，透過London Bridge 2 PCC發行£1.4億巨災債，讓投資人承擔Lloyd's市場承保的風險。洪災理賠增加之下，Flood Re計畫繼續發行；英國央行旗下監理部門則考慮加速審批，包括部分ILS結構以十天為核准目標。不過，全球逾90%的ILS仍在百慕達掛牌，倫敦仍需更多持續發行與更快的執行，才能延續這筆交易的成果。

## 紐西蘭升息，日本債息與日圓也加大政策壓力

紐約開盤前，全球債券殖利率已在上升。英國10年期公債上升10個基點至4.95%，創近一個月高點。紐西蘭將官方現金利率調高25個基點至2.5%，為三年來首次升息，並表示可能需要繼續撤除刺激。通膨仍高於目標，經濟活動預期轉強，決策帶動紐幣與本地殖利率上升。

日本10年與20年期殖利率升至1996年以來最高，日圓在每美元約162.42附近，接近四十年低點。年度經濟計畫修訂草案改以貨幣政策支持物價穩定上升的措辭，淡化先前被視為阻礙日本央行升息的表述。日圓疲弱增加進口物價壓力之際，這項改動給央行更大的政策空間。

即使日本央行已將政策利率升至1%，6月銀行放款仍年增6.3%，為2020年8月以來最快。實質政策利率仍為負，信貸成長也顯示金融情勢尚未普遍轉緊，支持進一步正常化的理由。本地債券殖利率提高，也可能改變日本投資人對海外債券的相對價值判斷。

財政資金來源卻仍不清楚。首相高市早苗的計畫涵蓋14年、逾¥370兆公私部門投資，融資細節尚未確定，對財政整頓的明確表述也已刪除。穆迪維持A1評等與穩定展望，認為經濟成長、通膨及已有進展，可使債務占GDP由2020年度約219%，降至2030年低於195%。這項較有利的債務比率預測，仍未回答經常性支出、國防需求及日本央行減少購債後的資金缺口如何支應。

歐洲方面，羅馬尼亞在通膨超過10%的情況下，維持政策利率6.5%；波蘭則連續第四次會議維持3.75%。儘管6月通膨降至2.5%，波蘭仍將2026年通膨預測區間由1.6%至2.9%，上調至2.4%至3.3%。各國物價起點不同，能源風險卻同樣使降息更難推進。

中國公債標售的強勁買盤，來自另一種環境。10年期標售的一項需求指標創紀錄，平均得標殖利率1.7249%、最高1.7418%，接近次級市場約1.728%。民間信貸需求不足，銀行轉而爭取公債配置；這反映本地放款機會有限，而非全球同步轉向存續期間資產。

## 阿根廷備妥還款資金，孟加拉研究首度海外發債

新興市場美元債承受較高美債實質殖利率，卻未同時遭遇美元走強。EMB下跌0.16%，美元指數則下跌0.09%至101.05。各借款人的現金來源與融資選擇，比一致性的美元流動性緊縮更能解釋差異。

阿根廷表示，已備妥外幣債券半年度本金與利息合計$43億的支付資金。財政部持有約$40億美元存款，另有多邊機構支持的款項預計在週四到期前到位。自3月以來，境內美元債已籌得約$40億；官員也指出，有其他融資安排可望讓政府直到2027年底都不必重返國際債市。

提前籌資降低了眼前的展期風險，並避開官員認為過高的外部融資利率。後續還款仍有賴境內美元買盤、官方融資及穩定的現金準備；支付這次到期款，不等於已建立可持續使用的國際市場管道。

孟加拉則研究相反的路徑：首度發行海外主權債，分散對本地銀行及優惠貸款的依賴。跨部會小組將評估結構、時機與可行性，以一般美元債為主，也討論熊貓債，規模與幣別尚未決定。預算支出計畫年增19%之際，首發可為企業建立定價指標，也會讓政府財政與改革紀錄接受外部投資人檢驗。

約翰尼斯堡擬透過清償債權人，恢復遭扣留的R36億政府資金，並討論發債修復基礎設施。後續撥款的條件包括：安排支付債權人款項，並提出計畫，在9月底前將未經授權、違規及浪費性支出至少減少25%。建設需求迫切，但債券發行仍須以恢復移轉收入及可信的支出管理為基礎。

智利通膨則使降息期待更複雜。6月物價持平，未如預期下降0.2%，年增率反而加速至4.3%，高於3%目標；能源與交通降價，食品卻上漲。市場仍反映六個月內降息25個基點的部分機率，因此燃料降價之外的物價壓力能否緩解，仍影響本地債市。

## 油價與波動率上升，科技股卻收復跌勢

美股收復大部分早盤失土。S&P 500盤中最多下跌1.1%，終場跌幅縮至0.28%；Nasdaq 100上漲0.27%，半導體上漲2.23%。能源業者受惠於油價，科技股則有逢低買盤。VIX上升4.77%至16.90，但相較衝突再起，絕對水準仍有限。

油價是跨市場最顯著的變動。WTI收在$73.52、布蘭特收在$78.02，進一步收復過去一個月的大幅跌勢。美國撤銷銷售豁免時，約6,300萬桶伊朗原油已在海上；銷售與航運限制威脅供應可得性，汽油及蒸餾油庫存下降則提高下游對中斷的敏感度。

黃金沒有因地緣消息受惠，反而下跌1.79%至$4,070.90。實質殖利率升高，增加持有不生息資產的機會成本，加上部位調整壓力，壓過即時避險買盤。即使Fed升息預期提前，美元指數也回落至101.05，兩者都不符合全面搶進避險資產的走勢。

科技股的反差最明顯：債券下跌、原油大漲之際，半導體卻反彈。股票與高收益債尚未反映全面性的成長衝擊；若能源中斷持續，進一步推升廣泛物價並迫使政策更緊，這種韌性就會受到更大考驗。

## 就業、通膨與長債標售接棒

7月9日美東08:30公布初領失業救濟金，10:00公布成屋銷售；6月CPI與實質所得則於7月14日08:30公布。就業與房市可補充循環信貸減速的背景，核心及非能源CPI細項則有助判斷，油價是否正在加重原本就持續的通膨。實質所得也能呈現家庭購買力受到的壓力。

財政部將於7月9日美東13:00增額發行$220億、票息5%的30年期公債，剩餘天期29年10個月，與週三發行的10年期券同於7月15日交割。相對發行前交易的得標殖利率、直接及間接投標人參與、交易商承接比例與後續走勢，將顯示本週公司債大量供給後，指標券的強勁需求能否延伸至長債。

日本央行區域報告與馬來西亞央行決策將於7月9日公布，7月10日則有德國CPI終值及加拿大就業報告。日本放款與公債殖利率已升高，區域薪資與企業定價訊息尤其值得留意。這些結果也有助分辨，紐西蘭升息是更廣泛緊縮趨勢的一部分，還是較偏向本國條件。

overall_summary.headline: 油價與偏鷹Fed紀錄推升殖利率，長債仍有買盤
overall_summary.session_narrative:
停火動搖帶動布蘭特上漲5.21%，6月Fed紀錄也顯示，少數官員當時已認為有理由升息。5年期美債領跌，殖利率上升4個基點至4.31%；10年期上升1個基點至4.56%，完全來自實質利率，損益兩平通膨率維持2.25%。

$390億10年期增額標售的得標殖利率低於發行前交易約0.6個基點，投標倍數2.59。信用保護成本升高之際，QTS尋求以完工資料中心融資，中東發行人使用私募，Flood Re也完成倫敦巨災債。Aston Martin與Victoria卻面對更艱難的債權人協商。

紐西蘭升息至2.5%。日本殖利率與放款成長上升、日圓仍弱，使正常化持續受到關注，財政資金來源卻未定。阿根廷備妥下一筆還款，孟加拉研究首度海外發債。7月9日將公布失業救濟金與房市資料，並進行30年期美債增額標售。
overall_summary.summary: 5年期美債殖利率上升4個基點至4.31%，10年期僅上升1個基點至4.56%。市場將下一次預期升息提前至10月，強勁的增額標售需求則限制指標券跌幅。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Oil and Fed Minutes Lift the Belly; Auction Demand Holds the Long End

Treasury yields rose again Wednesday as oil rallied and the June Fed minutes kept another increase in rates in play. The selloff was smaller than Tuesday's and concentrated at five years, where the yield rose 4 basis points to 4.31%. The 10-year added just 1 to 4.56% after a well-bid $39 billion reopening.

Brent gained 5.21% as the US-Iran ceasefire faltered, while depleted fuel inventories left less protection against disruption. The minutes showed that a few officials had already seen a case for raising rates in June, despite the unanimous decision to hold. Money markets brought the next expected hike forward to October. Ten-year inflation compensation nevertheless stayed at 2.25%; the small benchmark yield increase came entirely through real yield.

Investors still bought duration at the higher yields. The Treasury auction cleared below pre-sale trading, and US equities recovered much of an early decline. Credit protection costs widened, but funding remained available through private placements, asset-backed loans and specialist structures. Distressed borrowers faced a different market: Aston Martin's creditors organized as its notes fell, and Victoria offered bondholders a restructuring with large losses for those who declined.

## Five-Year Treasuries Bear the Brunt of Earlier Hike Pricing

The two-year yield rose 2 basis points to 4.21%, five years added 4 to 4.31%, and 10 and 30 years each rose 1 to 4.56% and 5.06%. Both 2s10s and 2s30s narrowed 1 basis point, to 35 and 85. Five-year underperformance, rather than a renewed surge in long yields, distinguished Wednesday from the previous day's broad selloff.

At 10 years, real yield increased 1 basis point to 2.31%, leaving breakeven inflation unchanged at 2.25%. Five-year real yield also rose 1 to 2.00%, seven years held at 2.14%, and 20 and 30 years added 1 and 2 to 2.66% and 2.86%. Oil was reshaping expectations for the Fed without lifting the day's measured 10-year inflation compensation.

The June 16–17 minutes described elevated upside risks to prices and slightly reduced downside risks to employment. A few participants saw a case for an increase, though all voted to hold the funds range at 3.5%–3.75%. Nine officials projected at least one 25-basis-point increase in 2026, including six who expected at least two; the other nine foresaw no change or a cut. Chair Kevin Warsh did not submit a forecast.

The committee had not settled on an unconditional hiking path. Most could envisage holding or eventually cutting if inflation moderated, but most also regarded some firming as likely if AI-driven demand, energy and tariffs kept prices rising too quickly. They still expected solid real growth and a stable labor market. Renewed hostilities made that inflation risk more immediate, bringing the next expected hike forward to October in market pricing.

US strikes and restrictions on Iranian oil sales aggravated the energy outlook. WTI rose 4.37% to $73.52, while Brent finished at $78.02 after trading above $79. In the week ended July 3, commercial crude inventories rose 3.0 million barrels, but gasoline stocks fell 1.9 million and distillates dropped 5.0 million. Distillate inventories were about 12% below their five-year seasonal average even with refinery utilization at 95.8%. The crude build offered little reassurance about the availability of finished fuels.

Domestic releases were less one-sided. May wholesale sales increased 3.4% to $817.4 billion after April's gain was revised to 2.2%. Inventories rose only 0.1% to $941.8 billion, taking the inventories-to-sales ratio to 1.15 from 1.31 a year earlier. Turnover remained strong relative to stocks, although nominal sales alone could not distinguish volume from price increases.

Consumer borrowing slowed sharply. Total credit was unchanged at a seasonally adjusted annual rate after April's revised 4.9% increase. Revolving credit contracted at a 4.7% annual rate, while nonrevolving credit grew 1.6%; outstanding credit totaled $5.1545 trillion. The decline in card borrowing raised a question about consumption resilience under higher rates, even though oil and the Fed dominated the day's trading.

### Benchmark Buyers Take the Concession

The $39 billion 10-year reopening was awarded at 4.580%, about 0.6 basis points below pre-auction trading, with 2.59 bid-to-cover. Indirect bidders received $31.721 billion, direct bidders $4.175 billion and dealers $3.027 billion. The note has nine years and 10 months remaining and settles July 15. Strong investor participation limited benchmark losses without producing a broader rally.

Treasury also sold $72 billion of 119-day bills at a 3.790% high rate, drawing 3.41 bid-to-cover. Indirect awards were $48.986 billion, compared with $3.158 billion for direct bidders and $18.227 billion for dealers; settlement is July 14. The secondary 17-week yield rose 2 basis points to 3.89%, while four-, six- and eight-week yields fell. Cash demand remained firm even as the policy-sensitive part of the curve cheapened.

## Funding Finds New Routes as Credit Investors Become More Selective

Credit-default swap spreads widened after the ceasefire rupture. LQD fell 0.19%, HYG 0.13% and JNK 0.16%, relatively limited losses beside the renewed oil move. Tight valuations left little cushion for event risk, but borrowers could still find funding through a growing range of mandates and structures.

US nontraditional bond-fund assets had expanded about 6% in 2026 and 18% since the end of 2024; European global flexible-bond assets were almost 10% higher for the year. Such managers can move beyond expensive benchmark sectors, giving issuers another pool of demand while increasing the importance of security selection.

Middle Eastern borrowers were turning to private placements. CEEMEA volume reached roughly $33 billion in 2026, about 10 times the year-earlier pace, with Middle Eastern sovereigns, companies and financial institutions accounting for around two-thirds. Qatar Energy's $3.5 billion June transaction illustrated the scale available away from public markets. Speed and confidentiality carried a cost: the average private-placement coupon in the first half was 5.12%, against 3.18% for internationally sold EM bonds, consistent with an illiquidity premium rather than cheaper funding.

New analysis put a price on the previous day's Amazon supply. Bank of America's Yuri Seliger and Sohyun Marie Lee estimated that the transaction widened outstanding hyperscaler spreads by 6–15 basis points and added 8 basis points to Tuesday's 10-year Treasury yield increase. That Treasury figure was their estimated contribution, not a decomposition of the official daily change. Amazon's roughly $41 billion book covered the $25 billion sale 1.6 times, versus 4.7 times for its February deal. The company had issued over $90 billion that year, within a $194 billion hyperscaler tally. Those supply totals have a narrower scope than the broader global AI-bond figures reported earlier.

### Completed Assets Support Borrowing; Distressed Issuers Cede Value

Blackstone-owned QTS sought $2 billion to refinance US data-center debt and pay dividends. The package included a $1 billion term loan offered at 99–99.5 with a margin of 225–250 basis points, plus another $1 billion of secured debt. Collateral comprised 12 completed data centers fully leased to three investment-grade hyperscalers. Contracted cash flow from operating assets supported the borrowing, unlike financing dependent on unfinished construction and future demand.

Cantor Fitzgerald arranged a proposed $300 million First Abu Dhabi Bank facility for Seer Capital purchases of significant-risk-transfer instruments, supported by investment-grade insurance guarantees. At more than 50% of investment net asset value, the facility could support exposure linked to at least $4 billion of bank loans. Insurance reduced financing costs, but the underlying instruments absorbed 5%–15% of portfolio losses. Leverage increased dependence on loan performance and the strength of the guarantees.

Aston Martin's creditors were preparing for a more difficult outcome. An ad hoc group holding over half its senior secured notes signed a cooperation agreement as earnings pressure drove debt lower. Its $1.05 billion of 2029 secured notes traded near 72 cents, down about 4 cents Wednesday. Senior security did not protect the notes from deteriorating operations; recovery value and creditors' negotiating position were becoming central.

Victoria offered consenting holders of its 2028 notes 75% of their value in new second-priority 2031 bonds, plus roughly 19% of the equity. The restructuring would reduce debt and preferred-share liabilities by more than £300 million. Holdouts faced a write-down to zero. Funding relief came through a redistribution of claims and ownership, not simply a longer maturity at a higher coupon.

London's insurance-linked market supplied a separate completed transaction. Flood Re, Britain's flood insurer of last resort, issued a £140 million catastrophe bond through London Bridge 2 PCC, giving investors exposure to risks underwritten in the Lloyd's market. It intended further issuance as flood claims increased. The BOE's regulatory arm was considering faster approvals, including a 10-day target for some ILS structures, but more than 90% of global ILS listings still occurred in Bermuda. Repeated issuance and faster execution would be needed to build on the initial London deal.

## New Zealand Hikes as Japan's Yields and Yen Pull Policy in the Same Direction

Global yields were rising before New York opened. Ten-year gilts added 10 basis points to 4.95%, their highest in almost a month. New Zealand raised its Official Cash Rate 25 basis points to 2.5%, its first increase in three years, and signaled that further withdrawal of stimulus might be needed. Inflation remained above target and activity was expected to strengthen. The currency and local yields rose.

In Japan, 10- and 20-year yields reached their highest levels since 1996, while the yen traded near 162.42 per dollar, close to a 40-year low. A revised draft of the annual economic plan referred to monetary policy supporting stable price increases, softening earlier language interpreted as discouraging BOJ tightening. The change gave the central bank more latitude as currency weakness added to imported-price pressure.

Bank lending grew 6.3% in June from a year earlier, the fastest since August 2020, despite the BOJ's increase in its policy rate to 1%. With real policy rates still negative, credit growth suggested that financial conditions had not become broadly restrictive. That evidence supported further normalization, while higher domestic bond yields could alter Japanese investors' comparisons with foreign duration.

Fiscal funding remained less clear. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's plan envisaged more than ¥370 trillion of public and private investment over 14 years, without settled financing details. An explicit reference to fiscal consolidation had been removed. Moody's retained its A1 rating and stable outlook, citing growth, inflation and progress that could lower debt below 195% of GDP by 2030 from about 219% in fiscal 2020. The favorable debt-ratio projection did not explain how recurring spending, defense needs and reduced BOJ purchases would be financed.

Elsewhere, Romania held at 6.5% with inflation above 10%, while Poland kept rates at 3.75% for a fourth meeting. Poland raised its 2026 inflation forecast range to 2.4%–3.3% from 1.6%–2.9%, even after June inflation slowed to 2.5%. Higher energy risk delayed easing in economies with very different starting points.

China's sovereign auction found unusually strong demand for a different reason. A 10-year sale reached a record demand gauge and cleared at an average 1.7249%, with a high yield of 1.7418%, near the roughly 1.728% secondary level. Banks sought government bonds amid insufficient private credit demand. The local bid reflected limited alternatives for lending, rather than a common global shift into duration.

## Argentina Prefunds Its Payment While Bangladesh Studies a Debut

Emerging-market dollar bonds faced higher Treasury real yields without an accompanying dollar surge. EMB fell 0.16%, while DXY slipped 0.09% to 101.05. Borrowers' access to cash and their chosen funding channels mattered more than a uniform squeeze in dollar liquidity.

Argentina said it had secured funding for a $4.3 billion semiannual principal-and-interest payment on foreign-currency bonds. Treasury held about $4 billion in dollar deposits, with multilateral-backed proceeds due before Thursday's maturity. Locally issued dollar bonds had raised roughly $4 billion since March. Officials also identified financing intended to keep the country out of international bond markets through the end of 2027.

Prefunding reduced the immediate rollover risk and avoided external yields officials considered too expensive. Later payments would still depend on domestic dollar buyers, official financing and durable cash reserves; meeting this maturity did not establish repeatable international market access.

Bangladesh was exploring the opposite route: a first overseas sovereign bond to diversify beyond domestic banks and concessional loans. An inter-ministerial panel would assess structure, timing and feasibility, focusing on conventional dollar debt while also discussing a Panda bond. Neither size nor currency had been decided. With planned spending up 19% from a year earlier, a debut could establish a corporate pricing benchmark while subjecting the sovereign's fiscal and reform record to external scrutiny.

Johannesburg planned creditor payments to restore R3.6 billion of withheld government funding and was discussing an infrastructure bond. Further disbursements depended on a plan to reduce unauthorized, irregular and wasteful spending by at least 25% by the end of September, alongside arrangements to pay creditors. Repair needs were large, but a sale would also require restored transfers and credible spending controls.

Chilean inflation complicated hopes for easing. June prices were flat against forecasts for a 0.2% decline, and annual inflation accelerated to 4.3%, above the 3% target. Food rose while energy and transport fell. Markets still assigned some probability to a quarter-point cut within six months, leaving local bonds sensitive to whether the broader price pressure persisted after fuel relief.

## Technology Recovers Even as Oil and Volatility Rise

US equities regained much of their early losses. The S&P 500 finished down 0.28% after falling as much as 1.1%, while Nasdaq 100 rose 0.27% and semiconductors gained 2.23%. Energy producers benefited from higher crude, and technology attracted dip buyers. VIX rose 4.77% to 16.90, still a contained level despite the renewed conflict.

Oil remained the largest cross-market move. WTI ended at $73.52 and Brent at $78.02, reversing more of their substantial monthly losses. Around 63 million barrels of Iranian oil were already at sea when the US revoked the sales waiver. Restrictions on its sale and shipping threatened availability, while gasoline and distillate inventory declines increased sensitivity to disruption downstream.

Gold fell 1.79% to $4,070.90 despite the geopolitical news. Higher real yields raised the cost of holding the non-yielding asset, and positioning pressure outweighed immediate haven demand. The dollar also eased to 101.05 despite earlier Fed-hike pricing. Neither move resembled a broad rush for protection.

The contrast was clearest in technology: semiconductors rallied while bonds weakened and oil surged. Equities and high-yield funds had not priced a generalized growth shock. Their resilience would be harder to sustain if the energy disruption lasted long enough to feed into broader prices and a more restrictive policy path.

## Labor, Inflation and the Long-Bond Sale Come Next

Initial claims arrive July 9 at 08:30 ET, followed by existing-home sales at 10:00. June CPI and real earnings are due July 14 at 08:30. Labor and housing will add context to the slowdown in revolving credit; core and non-energy CPI detail will show whether oil is compounding persistent inflation. Real earnings will help gauge the pressure on household purchasing power.

Treasury reopens $22 billion of the 5% 30-year bond July 9 at 13:00 ET, with 29 years and 10 months remaining. Settlement is July 15 alongside Wednesday's 10-year note. Auction pricing versus when-issued yields, direct and indirect participation, dealer retention and subsequent trading will show whether the benchmark's strong demand extends to the long bond after the week's corporate supply.

The BOJ regional report and Bank Negara Malaysia decision follow July 9, then German final CPI and Canada's labor report July 10. Japan's wage and price-setting evidence is particularly relevant after the rise in bank lending and JGB yields. The releases will also show whether New Zealand's hike belongs to a broader tightening trend or reflects more country-specific conditions.
